actions.action: Prune fully yellow/brown or mostly dead leaves at the base
Trim only the dead brown edges of leaves if they bother you
Acclimate gradually if moving to a sunnier spot
Check soil and water thoroughly when top 2–5 cm is dry
Feed with balanced fertilizer every 2–4 weeks in spring/summer
Make sure the pot has drainage holes
Repot every 2–3 years or when roots crowd the pot
Move to a more sheltered spot if very wind-exposed
Bring indoors to sunniest window before temps drop below 10 °C
Check leaf undersides and stem bases for spider mites and scale
Wipe leaves with a damp cloth
Post a close-up if yellowing, mushy stems or crispy leaves appear

reason: The answer notes the worn lower leaves but calls them normal aging and limits pruning to fully dead leaves, so it only partly matches the fix of cutting the damaged lower leaves; it also calls the pot a good size, contradicting the repot suggestion, though nothing it recommends is likely to hurt the plant.
